title: Cosimo's studio sound, then the ILA dance with Earl King and Cato
summary: Ridgley, Earl King and Cato had hot records, played the ILA hall for McKinley, and he charged $150 for ten pieces.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh, the going across the river, was that done at Cosmos and for some reason it doesn't... I'm going across that river? Yeah. Oh, you haven't done that Cosmos? I was just wondering, for some reason it didn't sound... Sometimes Cosmos Studio sound sort of changes at different periods.

Cosmos would luck up and get one, you know, and then he'd miss, and then he'd luck up and get another. But when he was on Dumaine Street, see that was when we all, everything sounded like it was in a little box, although the fat man came out of there. And Jewel King, three times seven, and a lot of other things. But then he moved on Governor Nichols. Right. Okay, this was when the studio was much bigger, you know, and I think this was when the sound kind of evolved to be better. And I did a lot of things over there with, for Rick. That's why all the tunes on Rick records sound pretty good. They sound pretty good, sound-wise. And you know, I said I was always unlucky, because I had in the same old way, Earl King had Frick Bay, Kato had Mother-in-Law. All three of us, our records were hot in New Orleans. And Larry McKinley had this show with me, Earl King, and Kato at the ILA. That was the black dance hall. Boy, they had wall to wall, no chairs, no tables, just people like that. And Larry had told me, he said, man, look, I want you to give me a break. And back then I had to bring in ten pieces. I'm telling you, this is true, too. I had ten musicians, and I charged Larry a hundred and fifty dollars. And Larry told me, he said, man, look, if everything, if everything go all right, he said, you know, I'm going to take care of you. I don't think I ever told you this either, before. Okay, when the band, boy, with all them people in there, when we, and we just literally totally joined up. You know, because the three of us local, we had all of that hot records. I went in there, right from off the bandstand, because we were in the back, we went, I went through that door, and they had a desk. Larry had, that whole desk was full of money. He had a box, a paper box, cardboard box, full of money. All of the drawers were full of money. And, uh, gave me a hundred and fifty dollars. I said, man, you know, you told me he was going to take care of me. I hold my right hand of God on this. Larry fished through that money and found a ten dollar bill and gave to him. You hear what I'm saying? He found a ten dollar bill. And I could never believe it. You see, that's why, you know, I never have confidence in Larry, you see, because I know what Larry did to Cato. See, Larry McKinley is responsible for Cato being the way Cato is today. Let me tell you something.
